title: Doors, hinges and hardware upkeep
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: Queensland Government (Fair Trading), Apply for a security equipment installer licence (last updated 21 October 2026); NSW Police Force (SLED), Locksmith licensing FAQ (Class 2C) (no date shown).
audience: Handyman workers and locksmith and door installation workers at the basic level
learningOutcomes: Diagnose common door faults: sticking, rubbing, sagging, loose hinges and worn closers.
Decide what minor upkeep is within scope, and what must be referred, including fire and security doors.
Price and record door upkeep so the higher-rate work is clearly scoped.

instruction.heading: Diagnose the door before adjusting it
instruction.body: Most sticking or rubbing doors have one of a few causes: a loose or sagging hinge, a screw pulled out of the frame, a door out of square, swelling from moisture, or a latch that does not line up with the strike plate. Check the gaps around the door, open and close it slowly, and watch where it binds. Check the hinges for play and the screws for tightness. A screw that spins in a worn hole needs a longer screw or a packed hole, not more force. A door that is out of square may need planing, which removes material and should be recorded.

instruction.heading: Minor upkeep and referral boundaries
instruction.body: Tightening loose screws, lubricating hinges, adjusting a latch strike, and replacing a worn door stop are minor upkeep. Adjusting or replacing a door closer, a fire-rated door or its hardware, or any security hardware that controls access, needs a check first. Security hardware, including locks and locking systems, may involve licensing rules. In Queensland, removing and reinstalling household locks needs a security equipment installer licence, except where the building is being constructed, repaired or renovated (Queensland Government page, last updated 21 October 2026). Installing basic security items while such works are underway is exempt on the same page. Refer any task that changes a lock, a fire door or a door closer. A fire door is part of a fire safety system, so do not alter its hardware by guesswork.

instruction.heading: Price the work and record the outcome
instruction.body: Upkeep of doors is often low in price per visit, and a worker can raise the rate by scoping the work properly. Write each task on the quote with its status: included, optional, or referred. Record the door's condition before and after, the parts used, and any defect that was not fixed. Do not quote a fire door or security hardware repair as minor upkeep. A quote that names the referral clearly is more credible and avoids disputes later.

procedure: Check the gaps, the hinges and the strike plate, and watch the door move through its full range.
Identify the cause of the fault and write it down.
Tighten or pack loose screws, and adjust the strike plate where that is the cause.
Stop and refer for any fire-rated door, any door closer adjustment beyond minor cleaning, or any security hardware change.
Record the before and after condition, the parts used and any unresolved defect.
Quote the work with each task marked as included, optional or referred.

workedExamples.situation: A client wants a quick adjustment to the closer on a fire-rated door in a shared hallway, saying the door slams.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Should the adjustment be done as part of a standard upkeep visit?
workedExamples.reasoning: No. The door is fire-rated, so its closer is part of the fire safety system. Refer the adjustment to a competent person, record the request and the referral, and quote the closer separately. A minor upkeep visit covers loose screws on the door, not closer adjustment on a fire-rated door.

equipmentAndPpe: Screwdriver set and drill with correct bits
Longer screws and filler for stripped holes
Plane or sander where the door must be trimmed
Eye protection and dust mask for planing

commonErrors.error: Adjusting a fire-rated door closer as minor upkeep.
commonErrors.prevention: Refer it to a competent person, and quote it separately.

commonErrors.error: Over-tightening a screw in a stripped hole.
commonErrors.prevention: Use a longer screw or pack the hole, and check the hinge is seated.

commonErrors.error: Pricing a security hardware change as a simple fix.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the state licence position before quoting, and refer security hardware changes.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Building work thresholds: in Queensland, building work valued over $3,300 needs a QBCC licence. In Victoria, domestic building work with a contract worth more than $10,000 needs registration as a building practitioner, and re-blocking, re-stumping, demolishing or removing a home needs registration at any value. Work above these limits needs the licence or registration. This lesson does not grant either one.

Queensland: installing basic security items while a building is built, repaired or renovated is exempt. Removing and reinstalling household locks needs a security equipment installer licence, except where the building is being constructed, repaired or renovated (Queensland Government page, last updated 21 October 2026).
New South Wales: the NSW Police SLED page (no date shown) treats the Class 2C licence as the requirement for individual locksmiths.
Confirm with the Licensing and Regulation Division before accepting lock or door work.
Fire doors and their hardware are referred to a competent specialist. Completing this lesson does not give a locksmith licence, a security licence or any authority to alter fire-rated doors.

qualityStandard: The cause of each door fault is identified and recorded before adjustment.
Every fire-rated door or security hardware item is referred, not adjusted as minor upkeep.
The quote marks each task as included, optional or referred.
documentationEvidence: Door condition record, before and after, with the parts used
Quote showing included, optional and referred tasks
Referral note for any fire-rated or security item
summary: Diagnose the door before adjusting it, and tighten or pack loose fixings where that is the cause.
Refer fire doors, door closers beyond minor upkeep, and security hardware.
Quote and record each task with its status, so the higher-rate work is clearly scoped.

knowledgeChecks.question: A client asks for a quick closer adjustment on a fire-rated door. What is the correct response?
options: Adjust it because it is quick and the client is waiting at the door
Remove the closer and check it at home before returning it
Tell the client the door is fine without checking it on the day
Refer the adjustment to a competent person, and quote it separately

knowledgeChecks.question: A screw spins in a worn hole in the hinge. What is the best approach?
options: Use a longer screw or pack the hole, then check the hinge is seated
Tighten harder until it grips, since more force usually fixes a loose screw
Leave it because it will not move once the screw is fully in place
Drill a new hole in the frame without checking the frame first

knowledgeChecks.question: In Queensland, which statement about removing and reinstalling household locks is supported by the source?
options: It never needs a licence, since removing and refitting is a simple job
It needs a licence unless the building is under construction, repair or renovation
It needs a QBCC plumbing licence, since the locks are part of the plumbing system
It is exempt in all cases, so the worker can carry out the work at any site
